questions.stem: （第 1 空）
questions.explanation:
【答案】
[ B ] prone固定搭配
【线索】
to earthquakes and tsunamis 锁定"易遭受"语义
线索就在本句内：is __(1)__ to earthquakes and tsunamis, which caused the city to __(2)__ sink——后半句说地震与海啸"导致城市下沉"，反推空处必须表达"易遭受地震海啸"，候选词须能与 to 搭配且承载"易受……影响"之义。
【选项】
A)relevant✗搭配虽通但语义跑偏
be relevant to 意为"与……相关"，是中性的"相关性"，无法表达"易遭受灾害"这一受害方向；放回is __(1)__ to earthquakes and tsunamis只会变成"与地震海啸有关"，与下半句"导致城市下沉"的因果不衔接。
B)prone✓be prone to 正中"易遭受"
be prone to + n. 是英语里的固定表达，意为"易于、有……倾向"，常用于易发自然灾害；代入后"该海域易遭受地震和海啸"，与下文caused the city to __(2)__ sink的因果链严丝合缝。
C)available✗对象错配
available to 一般搭配人或机构（对某人开放/可获得），与"地震海啸"这种自然灾害事件搭配不通；说"海域对地震海啸是可获得的"在中文里就立即露馅。
D)alien✗语义反向
be alien to 意为"与……格格不入、对……陌生"，恰恰是"不易遭受"的反向；与下半句因地震海啸而下沉的事实矛盾。
【验证】
代入后整句为"This area of the Aegean Sea is __(1)__ to earthquakes and tsunamis, which caused the city to __(2)__ sink"——"易遭受地震海啸→导致城市下沉"，与第一段交代沉没原因的脉络一致。

questions.stem: （第 2 空）
questions.explanation:
【答案】
[ C ] gradually词义辨析
【线索】
下句 slow sea level rise 直接呼应
跨句线索就在下一句：The slow sea level rise in the Mediterranean __(3)__ the city more than 3,000 years ago——"地中海缓慢的海平面上升"明确把沉没过程定性为长期、渐进，本空必须与"slow"同向。
【选项】
A)accidentally✗语义不对路
accidentally 强调"偶然"，但城市下沉是地质过程，不是偶发事件，与下句slow sea level rise的渐进性也不合。
B)frequently✗把一次性过程误读为反复事件
frequently 表"频繁"，意味着多次发生，但城市"下沉"是一个一次性的长期演变，并非反复；与 slow 也不同向。
C)gradually✓与 slow 同向、贴渐进过程
gradually "逐渐地"正是 slow sea level rise 的同义改写，把"下沉"刻画为长期渐进过程，与全段地质成因的语境完全吻合。
D)temporarily✗与事实相反
temporarily 表"暂时地"，而城市此后lay unseen below some 13 feet of water数千年，完全不是暂时性下沉；逻辑反向。
【验证】
代入后caused the city to __(2)__ sink→"导致城市逐渐下沉"，与下一句"地中海海平面的缓慢上升"形成同义复述，与本段整体的渐进成因链自洽。

questions.stem: （第 3 空）
questions.explanation:
【答案】
[ B ] submerged词义辨析
【线索】
上句已说城市下沉、下段又说在水下
线索跨句：上一句caused the city to __(2)__ sink+下一段the city's __(4)__ lay unseen below some 13 feet of water共同把城市的最终状态钉死为"沉没于水下"，本空必须表达"海水使城市被淹没"。
【选项】
A)disguised✗对象不对
disguise 意为"伪装、掩饰"，主语通常是有意图的施动者或具有遮盖功能的物，且与城市下沉的物理过程不搭。
B)submerged✓正中"淹没"语义
submerge "使没入水中"恰好对应海平面上升将城市"淹没"的物理过程，与下一段lay unseen below some 13 feet of water的结果状态完全衔接。
C)relocated✗把"淹没"误读为"搬迁"
relocate 表"重新安置、迁移"，城市的位置并未改变，是水位上升把城市淹了；语义错位。
D)isolated✗范围对不上
isolate "使孤立"侧重切断联系，与海水彻底覆盖城市的物理事实不匹配。
【验证】
代入后"地中海缓慢上升的海平面在3000多年前淹没了这座城市"，与下一段开头For millennia, the city's __(4)__ lay unseen below some 13 feet of water衔接，前因后果一致。

questions.stem: （第 4 空）
questions.explanation:
【答案】
[ C ] remains词义辨析
【线索】
下文清点建筑、街道、墓室
跨段呼应：The team identified some 15 buildings, courtyards, a network of streets, and two chamber tombs与Pavlopetri's three main roads __(18)__ some 50 rectangular buildings说明水下保留的是建筑与街道，本空必须表"遗迹/遗存"。
【选项】
A)legends✗抽象项不合"沉于水下"
legends 是"传说"，属语言/叙述层面，不能物理上"lay below water"；与下文清点的实物（建筑、街道）也对不上。
B)programs✗范畴跑偏
programs "项目/计划/节目"是抽象事务，不能沉在海底；与本段历史遗存语境无关。
C)remains✓"遗迹/遗存"正解
remains 表"遗迹、遗存"，正好涵盖15 buildings, courtyards, a network of streets, and two chamber tombs这些被发掘的实物，能与"lay unseen below water"自然搭配。
D)surroundings✗指向错对象
surroundings 指"周围环境"，强调外围而非城市本体，但本段要谈的是城市自身被埋的部分（建筑、街道、墓室），不是周边环境。
【验证】
代入后"数千年里，这座城市的遗迹长期沉于约13英尺水下而无人察觉"，紧接其后They were covered by a thick layer of sand的代词 They 也恰好指代"remains"，前后衔接顺畅。

questions.stem: （第 5 空）
questions.explanation:
【答案】
[ B ] off固定搭配
【线索】
上一段已交代位于希腊本土近海
线索来自第一段开头Located in the southern Peloponnesian peninsula, Pavlopetri——遗址位于伯罗奔尼撒半岛南端近海，沙层位于"拉科尼亚岛沿岸/近海"，方位关系是"离岸不远"。
【选项】
A)across✗方向错
across 表"横跨"，意味着穿越岛屿或从一端到另一端，与"沙层位于岛屿附近海域"的实际方位不符。
B)off✓off + 岛屿名 = 近海
off the island of Laconia 是地理表达定式，意为"在拉科尼亚岛沿岸近海"，与全文"水下古城"的语境完美匹配。
C)under✗位置关系错配
under 意为"在……下方"，但沙层不可能位于整座岛屿下方；岛屿是陆地，与沙层是近海覆盖物的关系不同。
D)via✗搭配类型错
via 表"经由"，是路径介词，与静态位置描述无关。
【验证】
代入后"沙层覆盖物来自拉科尼亚岛沿岸/近海"，与第一段Located in the southern Peloponnesian peninsula的地理定位贯通。

questions.stem: （第 6 空）
questions.explanation:
【答案】
[ A ] currents词义辨析
【线索】
海洋环境下"shifting + 侵蚀屏障"指洋流
线索就在本句：shifting __(6)__ and climate change have eroded a natural barrier that __(7)__ Pavlopetri——海洋环境里能"shifting"并"侵蚀沿海屏障"的自然要素，是海流；季节/风/河流要么与海洋侵蚀不直接、要么搭 shifting 不自然。
【选项】
A)currents✓海流契合度最高
currents 既常与 shifting 搭配描述方向改变的洋流，又是侵蚀海岸屏障的直接动力，与下句eroded a natural barrier that __(7)__ Pavlopetri衔接最紧。
B)rivers✗场景错配
rivers 是河流，主要在陆地与河口起作用，而本句的屏障位于海洋一侧（保护已沉于地中海的遗址），用河流来"shifting"侵蚀这里的屏障不自然。
C)seasons✗搭配不通
shifting seasons 虽可指"季节更迭"，但季节本身不是直接侵蚀海岸屏障的物理力量，与 climate change 也几近重复。
D)winds✗次优但不及 currents
shifting winds 虽然可说，但风对水下沙层屏障的直接侵蚀作用不及洋流明显，且海洋语境里 currents 更对位。
【验证】
代入后"变化的海流与气候变化侵蚀了曾保护帕夫洛佩特里的天然屏障"，与下文eroded a natural barrier that __(7)__ Pavlopetri的因果一脉相承。

questions.stem: （第 7 空）
questions.explanation:
【答案】
[ D ] protected词义辨析
【线索】
前句"eroded barrier"暗含失去保护
线索就在主句：eroded a natural barrier that __(7)__ Pavlopetri——屏障被侵蚀，导致古城此后失去保护而暴露，反推屏障原本承担的是"保护"功能。
【选项】
A)elevated✗对宾语动作不当
elevate 表"抬高、提升"，屏障并未把古城"抬高"，与下沉于水下的事实矛盾。
B)separated✗侧重错位
separate 强调"使分离"，但本句要表达的是屏障"保护"古城免遭侵蚀，而非把古城与外界隔开；语义偏离主旨。
C)comprised✗主宾关系反了
comprise 意为"包含/构成"，屏障并未"包含"整座古城；逻辑关系不对。
D)protected✓屏障的本职功能

questions.material:
The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after
groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children’s literacy and emotional
development. But only if you act him out.
A study found that a “rehearsal room” approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened
children’s vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy. “The
research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language
and also how they think about themselves,” Jacqui O’Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company
(RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils — aged nine and ten — at
45 state primary schools that had not been “previously exposed to RSC pedagogy.” They were
split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as
Ferdinand following the shipwreck in The Tempest. The target group were given a 30-minute
drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary,
used words “classed as more sophisticated or rarer”, and wrote at greater length. They also
“appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they
themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a
literary character and express that character’s emotion”. The Time to Act study, which is
published by the RSC this week, also found that while control pupils relied on “desert island
clichés” such as palm trees, target pupils were “more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the
sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions”.
O’Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the “emotional literacy that was evident in the
[target] children’s writing” and that they were “more resilient in their writing, more hopeful”. She
added “The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal
room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable
in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in
different shoes.” The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O’Hanlon said more research
would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare’s use of 20,000 words, compared with the
everyday 2,000 words, gave a “massive expansion of language into children’s lives”, which was
combined with children “using their whole bodies to bring words to life”.
questions.stem: The “rehearsal room” approach requires pupils to ____
questions.explanation:
【答案】
C（细节题）
【判型】
题干 The "rehearsal room" approach requires pupils to___________. 是要求填具体做法的不完整陈述句，没有 infer/suggest/imply 之类推断信号词，属于典型细节题。
【拆句】
题干 The "rehearsal room" approach requires pupils to___________. 是一个待补全的陈述句，主语 The "rehearsal room" approach，谓语 requires，宾语 pupils，不定式 to ___ 是要填的部分，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】
P2
"The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC，本研究的委托方）的 Jacqui O'Hanlon 说："这项研究表明，演员的工作方式深深改变了孩子们使用语言的方式，也改变了他们对自己的认识。"
【选项】
A)无中生有
全文没有任何”重写/改写台词”的描述，rewrite 是凭空加上去的动作；这是利用题干”requires pupils to“求动作的预期，给一个看似合理但文中没有的动作。
B)偷换概念
原文要求孩子"act him out"亲身演出，而 watch RSC actors’ performances 把动作从"演"偷换成"看"——主动变被动，与原文意旨相反。
C)✓ 正确
the way actors work↔play the roles in Shakespeare
if you act him out↔play the roles in Shakespeare
预判要的就是"演"，C 选项 play the roles in Shakespeare 直接对应"演员工作方式"与"act him out"，是最干净的同义替换。
D)过度推断
原文 RSC 是研究的委托方，不是教学执行方；孩子是被引导用"演员方式"工作，不是"在 RSC 艺术家手下学戏剧"。该选项把研究合作关系夸大成”直接师从”。

questions.stem: The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether ____

options.text: the change in instruction enhances learning outcomes.
expanding vocabulary helps develop reading fluency.
emotion affects understanding of sophisticated works.
the classroom activity stimulates interest in the arts.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
A（细节题）
【判型】
题干 The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether___________. 问的是分组实验本身要检验什么，可在原文中找到对应陈述，不需做跨段推断。
【拆句】
题干 The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether___________. 中 to find whether 是目的状语，whether 引导宾语从句，从句内容正是要填的部分；理解关键是看清”分组”是手段，”find whether ...“才是目的。
【定位】
P3
They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in *The Tempest*. The target group was given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
他们被分成 target（实验）组和 control（对照）组，被要求以《暴风雨》中船难之后的 Ferdinand 身份写一封”漂流瓶里的信”。target 组额外获得了一个 30 分钟的戏剧化活动来配合该段落。
【选项】
A)✓ 正确
a 30-minute drama-based activity↔the change in instruction
The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length.↔enhances learning outcomes
唯一变量是教学方式的改变，被观测的产出是写作/学习上的表现，A 选项把”变量→产出”的因果检验完整覆盖，与预判一致。
B)偷换概念
扩展词汇是该实验的部分结果之一，不是分组想检验的初衷；而且 reading fluency "阅读流畅度"原文从未提及，把写作产出偷换成阅读能力。
C)与原文相反

questions.material:
The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after
groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children’s literacy and emotional
development. But only if you act him out.
A study found that a “rehearsal room” approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened
children’s vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy. “The
research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language
and also how they think about themselves,” Jacqui O’Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company
(RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils — aged nine and ten — at
45 state primary schools that had not been “previously exposed to RSC pedagogy.” They were
split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as
Ferdinand following the shipwreck in The Tempest. The target group were given a 30-minute
drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary,
used words “classed as more sophisticated or rarer”, and wrote at greater length. They also
“appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they
themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a
literary character and express that character’s emotion”. The Time to Act study, which is
published by the RSC this week, also found that while control pupils relied on “desert island
clichés” such as palm trees, target pupils were “more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the
sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions”.
O’Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the “emotional literacy that was evident in the
[target] children’s writing” and that they were “more resilient in their writing, more hopeful”. She
added “The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal
room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable
in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in
different shoes.” The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O’Hanlon said more research
would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare’s use of 20,000 words, compared with the
everyday 2,000 words, gave a “massive expansion of language into children’s lives”, which was
combined with children “using their whole bodies to bring words to life”.

questions.explanation:

【判型】
题干 Control pupils' reliance on "desert island clichés" shows their ___________. 用 shows 把原文现象指向其反映的”特质”，需要从描写一步推到性质判断。
【拆句】
题干 Control pupils' reliance on "desert island clichés" shows their ___________. 主语是动名词性短语 Control pupils' reliance on ... clichés，谓语 shows，宾语 their ___ 待填；理解要点是 reliance on clichés“对陈词滥调的依赖”本身就是负面色彩，正确答案应延续这一负面方向。
【定位】
P5
The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions".
"是时候行动"研究还发现：control 组的学生只靠"沙漠岛俗套"（比如棕榈树）来写，而 target 组的学生"更加宏阔，呈现出关于天空、大海与大气状况的更广阔画面"。
【选项】
A)✓ 正确
relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees↔weakness in description
target pupils were "more expansive [giving a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions"]]↔weakness in description
陈词滥调一词本身就是写作描述贫弱的标准外显，A 选项与预判完全吻合。
B)无中生有
control 组不是"遗漏了小细节"，而是"画面单调"；原文反差是"狭窄 vs 宏阔"，不是"漏 vs 不漏"；而且 small details 在原文没有任何对应。

clichés 是明确负面的词，原文是在批评 control 组写作贫弱；casual style of writing 把这种负面评价淡化为"随意的写作风格"这一中性甚至略带褒义的描述，性质方向错。

preference for big words 描述的是"偏爱大词"——这正是 target 组的特征（words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer"），不是 control 组；而且 palm trees 显然不是 big words。

questions.stem: What can promote children’s emotional literacy according to O’Hanlon?
questions.explanation:
【答案】
B（细节题）
【判型】
题干 What can promote children's emotional literacy according to O'Hanlon? 限定到 O'Hanlon 的原话，需要在文中找她的引语，属人物观点细节题。
【拆句】
题干 What can promote children's emotional literacy according to O'Hanlon? 是一个 wh-疑问句，主语是疑问代词 What，谓语 can promote，according to O'Hanlon 是观点来源状语；理解关键是绑定 O'Hanlon 这一信源，不能用全文其他来源的描述代替。
【定位】
P6
She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes."
她补充道：“情感理解非常明显，这很可能与”排练室式过程”有关——在那种过程中，你习惯于一路靠想象去走通。他们能从容地描述各种不同的情绪状态，而戏剧的一部分就是把自己放进不同的鞋里（换位）。”

A)以偏概全

B)✓ 正确
put yourself in different shoes↔Identifying with literary characters.
[target children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion]]↔Identifying with literary characters.
原文反复强调”穿别人的鞋”+“代入文学角色”，B 选项用 identifying with literary characters 把这两层意思合二为一，与预判精准吻合。

Drawing inspiration from nature 取自 P5 a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions，那段讨论的是写作描述力，与情感素养的成因无关；O'Hanlon 没把情感素养归因于自然。

I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an
effort to decrease carbon emissions. The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our
energy-intensive modelling. At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more
sustainable.
It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites — the tools
we scientists need to measure the planet’s pulse — demand significant amounts of energy both in
their construction and operation. And it is equally true that science’s unrelenting appetite for
information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world.
According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 percent of
the world’s electricity.
However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. How can we inform
decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can’t track the amount
of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it’s coming from and who’s producing it? The carbon
emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the
future of our planet.
It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place
behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation. But
demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity’s greatest
challenges. It is all too easy to feel paralysed in the face of daunting problems such as climate
change and to do nothing. But then I think of a friend’s daughter who turned her fears into action:
she became a wind energy engineer and now thrives on delivering renewable energy, limiting
emissions.
Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the
creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration
of human ingenuity. One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New
South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which
is now found in most of the world’s solar panels. Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance
to decrease the world’s carbon emissions.
Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit
renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to
power our intelligence. A great example of this is Europe’s largest supercomputer, LUMI in
Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by
a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver
sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.
questions.stem: The author expressed great surprise at some scientists’ ____

options.text: waste of electricity in their projects.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
B（细节题）
【判型】
The author expressed great surprise at some scientists' ________. 问的是「作者对科学家的什么感到吃惊」，要的是一个具体事实而非推断。
【拆句】
主干是 The author expressed great surprise at some scientists'，空白处补的是 scientists' 后面的所有格名词，即「科学家的某种做法/想法」；'s 表所属，不是缩写。
【定位】
P1
I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions.
我最近吃惊地得知，一些科学家想要缩减他们的科研工作，以求降低碳排放。
【选项】
A)与原文相反
原文是科学家「想减碳→缩减科研」，unwillingness to cut carbon emissions 反过来说他们不愿减碳，与原文意图相反。
B)✓ 正确
scale back their research↔reduce their research
some scientists want to↔intention to
intention to reduce their research 把预判中的「想要」和「缩减科研」整对兑现，与定位句完全等值。
C)无中生有
首段只讲他们想 make our energy use far more sustainable，是赞成可持续，没有任何怀疑。
D)偷换概念
P2 只承认 significant amounts of energy 的高消耗，但不是浪费；首段更没有「浪费」之说。

questions.stem: The author believes that carbon emissions from research ____

options.text: are hard to handle at present.
are justifiable in the long run.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
D（细节题）
【判型】
The author believes that carbon emissions from research ________. 找的是作者直接陈述的观点，原文有明确语句对应，不需要跨段推断。
【拆句】
句子结构是 The author believes that + 从句；从句主语 carbon emissions from research 后面留空让你补谓语，因此选项给的是动词短语对该主语的评价。
【定位】
P3
However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. … The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.
然而，这是我们为理解世界必须付出的代价。……科技研究产生的碳排放是值得花的：归根到底，这些研究将守护我们星球的未来。
【选项】
A)与原文相反
原文只承认科研耗能大，但作者明确为之辩护；从未说它已造成 grave consequences。
B)无中生有
作者只为科研碳排辩护，没说担忧 groundless；他承认耗能事实，并不否认担忧本身。
C)偷换概念
作者关心的是长远价值，未提「目前难处理」；at present 是凭空加入的时间限定。
D)✓ 正确
are well spent↔are justifiable
ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet↔in the long run
are justifiable in the long run 同时落实了「值得」和「长远」两个核心要素，与作者评价句一一对应。

questions.stem: The example of Green in Paragraph 5 is used to illustrate ____

options.text: the urgency of addressing climate change.
the value of fostering human ingenuity.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
C（例证目的题）
【判型】
The example of Green in Paragraph 5 is used to illustrate ________. 显式使用 example…is used to illustrate 句式，要的是举例的「为何举」。
【拆句】
主干 The example…is used to illustrate ____；is used to do 是被动表「被用来做某事」，问的是举例的目的；介词短语 in Paragraph 5 修饰 example，限定该例的位置。
【定位】
P5
Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity.
正是出于对科学与工程所能带来希望的肯定，才有了千禧科技奖的设立；该奖如今已步入第 20 年，意在表彰人类的智慧创造。
【选项】
A)答非所问
原文确实写到 Green 的发明成就，但例证目的不是夸他个人，而是借「他得奖」来体现奖项的存在意义；选 A 等于把例子当成论点。
B)偷换概念
P5 末句虽说 Green 的发明给减碳带来 a real chance，但并未渲染气候 urgency；段落中心也不是讨论问题紧迫性。
C)✓ 正确
was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize↔the rewards of scientific endeavours
Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring↔the rewards of scientific endeavours
Green 是「获奖者」，其作用是体现「科研贡献被奖励」；the rewards of scientific endeavours 正是此中心论点的浓缩。
D)以偏概全
a celebration of human ingenuity 只是奖项的定语描述；段落真正的中心是「奖励/认可这种智慧带来的希望」，而非「培育智慧」。

questions.material:
Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a
profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars
each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was. But
the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip
a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on
their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins
approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing
Hollywood studios that’s working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have
cropped up in recent years.
Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital
piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. But now piracy involving illegal streaming
services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and
some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce’s Global Innovation Policy Center.
The global impact is about $71 billion annually.
“The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites
are not mom and pop operations,” says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA. “This
is organized crime.” Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier
to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in
Congress aimed at stopping online piracy. In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for
Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling
the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.
ACE says it’s helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126,
from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA’s support for a 2020 federal law that
made large-scale streaming of copyright material a serious crime.
Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services’ cumulative
loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years. “While there is some
optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by
2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline,” says analyst
Steve Hawley.

options.text: are confronted with a real threat.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
D（细节题）
【判型】
题干 According to Paragraph 1 明确指向段内陈述，要求复述事实而非推断。
【拆句】
legitimate streaming services ________ 是一个待补全的不完整陈述句，主语是 legitimate streaming services，空格处补谓语；四个选项分别提供不同动词短语，比较选项时只需看与主语在第一段事实是否匹配，结构本身无陷阱。
【定位】
P1

But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.

A)与原文相反
have drawn lessons from Hollywood 把 Hollywood 当 "被学习的对象"，但原文 taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood 明说是 Hollywood 跟 Netflix 学，方向恰好倒置。
B)与原文相反
have surpassed cable in revenue 直接说正版流媒体收入已超过有线电视；但原文 sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was 是 "担心永远赶不上有线电视"，恰好相反。
C)无中生有
are unpopular with advertisers 把广告商对正版流媒体的态度凭空塞进文本；第一段只提到非法网站从 ads and subscriptions 捞钱，未谈广告商对正版的好恶。

pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions↔are confronted with a real threat
has struggled to turn a profit in streaming↔are confronted with a real threat
预判中的两层 (自家亏损 + 被盗版扒) 直接对应 are confronted with a real threat：a real threat 同时覆盖盈利困境和盗版蚕食，是预判的最简概括。

questions.stem: It can be learned that streamers like Netflix ____

options.text: played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing.
reaped benefits from the war with digital pirates.
promised to become big job creators in the US.
used to collaborate with file-uploading platforms.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
A（推断题）
【判型】
题干 It can be learned that streamers like Netflix ________ 使用 It can be learned 引导，要求由原文事实出发做一步合理推论。
【拆句】
It can be learned that streamers like Netflix ________ 是 It can be learned that 引导宾语从句的不完整结构，主语 streamers like Netflix 在从句内，空格补从句谓语；like 在这里是介词 "诸如"，不是动词，基础薄弱考生易误读为 "喜欢"，须留意。
【定位】
P3
Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads.
起初，像 Netflix 这样的合法在线生意的崛起，其实帮助遏制了数字盗版，而当时的盗版主要靠文件上传维系。
【选项】
A)✓ 正确
Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads↔played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing
原文事实 "Netflix 帮助压制以文件上传为主的盗版" 一步推 "Netflix 在打击非法文件分享中扮演了角色"，正是 played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing。
B)与原文相反
reaped benefits from the war with digital pirates 是 "Netflix 从与盗版的对战中获利"；但原文里获利的是盗版方 (上一段 unintended winners… pirates)，Netflix 们反而 has struggled to turn a profit in streaming，正反角色颠倒。
C)无中生有
promised to become big job creators in the US 谈的是 Netflix 们承诺创造大量岗位；第三段只提 some 250,000 jobs 的损失，且是盗版造成的、不是 Netflix 承诺的就业贡献。
D)与原文相反
used to collaborate with file-uploading platforms 说 Netflix 曾与文件上传平台合作；但定位句 helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads 明示 Netflix 是 "遏制" 文件上传盗版，而非合作。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 4 that the MPA ____

options.text: was denied cooperation by Silicon Valley.
led a national protest against online piracy.
was urged to form an enforcement task force.
failed to win support from local authorities.

questions.explanation:

题干 It can be inferred from Paragraph 4 明示推断属性。

It can be inferred from Paragraph 4 that the MPA ________ 与 32 题结构同型，主语 the MPA，谓语待补；选项均为被动或主动短语，须分清动作发出者与承受者，否则会和 33 题 A、D 两项的施受方向搞反。

Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a
profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars
each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was. But
the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip
a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on
their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins
approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing
Hollywood studios that’s working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have
cropped up in recent years.
Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital
piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. But now piracy involving illegal streaming
services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and
some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce’s Global Innovation Policy Center.
The global impact is about $71 billion annually.
“The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites
are not mom and pop operations,” says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA. “This
is organized crime.” Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier
to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in
Congress aimed at stopping online piracy. In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for
Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling
the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.
ACE says it’s helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126,
from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA’s support for a 2020 federal law that
made large-scale streaming of copyright material a serious crime.
Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services’ cumulative
loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years. “While there is some
optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by
2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline,” says analyst
Steve Hawley.

Visit any antiques store and you’ll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a
brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964-1965 World’s Fair, the ephemera of
history. Yet these objects aren’t truly ephemeral, because they’re still here, decades, even
centuries later. Why? Because they’re tangible.
Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those
who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation? For millennia,
we’ve known what we’ve known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original
creators’ neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. At the time of
creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of
surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on.
Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation,
and access to information. Thus, librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over
can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches,
which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
Librarians’ selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by
holding up a cellphone and saying, “it’s all in here” as evidence that libraries are less vital for
researchers today. Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more
importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital
information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital
information requires a great deal more care than analog.
Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the
information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless.
Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? Without
constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps
historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replace analog.
As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the
night terrors of historians, and I’d be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution
currently exists. Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of
librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers
current and future. Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use
information. Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to
digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to
ply their trade, they won’t find it an impossible one.
questions.stem: The author mentions the artifacts from the past to ____

options.text: bring up the issue of preservation.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
C（例证目的题）
【判型】
题干 The author mentions the artifacts from the past to 用「mention X to do」结构，问的是举例服务于哪一个论点。
【拆句】
题干 The author mentions the artifacts from the past to 是一个待补全句，主干为 The author mentions ... to + 选项动词原形，to 引出目的状语，无陷阱。
【定位】
P1
Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible.
然而这些东西并非真正转瞬即逝，因为几十年甚至几百年后它们依然在这里。为什么？因为它们是有形的。
【选项】
A)把例子当主题的典型干扰
introduce the collection of antiques 把作者引子里 antiques store 当成主题；可作者讲古董店只是借场景举例，全文真正主题是保存，不是收藏。
B)无中生有
contrast them with everyday items 提到的「与日常物对比」原文从未出现，第一段只把 artifacts 视为留存样本，没有任何 everyday items 出现。
C)✓ 正确
Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible.↔bring up the issue of preservation
预判「引出保存议题」与 bring up the issue of preservation 在动词（引出 vs bring up）与宾语（议题 vs the issue of preservation）上一一对应，直接锁定 C。
D)偷换概念
comment on their historical value 谈历史价值；原文 Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral 讨论的是「为何能留存」，不是「它们有多少历史价值」。

questions.stem: Compared with digital objects, tangible artifacts ____

options.text: are less subject to their creators’ neglect.
convey information in a more direct way.
are less likely to suffer serious damage.

questions.explanation:
【答案】
B（细节题）
【判型】
题干 Compared with digital objects, tangible artifacts 不含 infer/imply 等推断信号，问的是作者直接陈述的对比属性。
【拆句】
题干 Compared with digital objects, tangible artifacts 中 Compared with digital objects 是过去分词短语作状语，逻辑主语是 tangible artifacts，主干仍是 tangible artifacts + 选项谓语。
【定位】
P2
The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information.
物件本身就是承载并传递信息的媒介。
【选项】
A)与原文相反
are less subject to their creators' neglect 称有形物较少被创作者忽视；原文 often despite their original creators' neglect 恰恰说有形物常在创作者疏忽下仍然留存，并未说创作者对它们更上心。
B)✓ 正确
The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information.↔convey information in a more direct way
其它三项谈的是 neglect/preservation/damage，全在「保存难度」维度，与定位句「传递机制」不在同一语义场，故 B 是唯一与预判匹配的。
C)与原文相反
require more intentional preservation 称有形物需要更刻意的保存；原文 At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation 恰说创作时没有刻意保存的努力，与选项相反。
D)无中生有
are less likely to suffer serious damage 说有形物不易受损；原文未在「受损程度」上比较有形与数字，第二段谈的是创作者保存意图与留存机会，不涉及损伤难度。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, librarians’ work may result in ____
questions.explanation:
【答案】
B（细节题）
【判型】
librarians' work may result in 问的是行为带来的具体结果，是段内客观信息的直接转述。
【拆句】
题干 According to Paragraph 3, librarians' work may result in 主干 work may result in + 选项名词性短语；情态动词 may 仅是缓和语气，不是推断信号。
【定位】
P3
Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, "it's all in here" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today.
图书馆员的无私付出反过来会害了我们——用户举起手机说「一切都在这里」，以此为据声称图书馆对今日的研究者已没那么重要。
【选项】
A)答非所问
oversupply of materials 指材料供过于求；原文 embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems 谈的是「检索难」（大海捞针），而非数量上的供过于求。且该句在第二段，不属于 Q38 限定的 Paragraph 3。
B)✓ 正确
libraries are less vital for researchers today↔undervaluation of libraries
预判「让用户贬低图书馆的价值」与 undervaluation of libraries 在主体（libraries）和动作（贬低/低估）上完全对应，因此锁 B。

researchers' underperformance 称研究者表现不佳；第三段只说用户「认为图书馆不重要」，未评价研究者本身的表现高低。

questions.stem: The “ZIP disk” is cited as an example to show ____

options.text: the hazard of retrieving files through unusual means.
the infeasibility of constantly migrating digital assets.
the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats.
the inconvenience of storing information on analog devices.

【答案】
C（例证目的题）
【判型】
The "ZIP disk" is cited as an example to show 直接点明本题问举例的目的。
【拆句】
题干 The "ZIP disk" is cited as an example to show 中被动语态 is cited 的施事是作者，to show 引出目的状语，主语 ZIP disk 加引号强调原词出现。

A)过度推断

questions.material:
Visit any antiques store and you’ll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a
brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964-1965 World’s Fair, the ephemera of
history. Yet these objects aren’t truly ephemeral, because they’re still here, decades, even
centuries later. Why? Because they’re tangible.
Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those
who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation? For millennia,
we’ve known what we’ve known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original
creators’ neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. At the time of
creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of
surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on.
Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation,
and access to information. Thus, librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over
can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches,
which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
Librarians’ selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by
holding up a cellphone and saying, “it’s all in here” as evidence that libraries are less vital for
researchers today. Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more
importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital
information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital
information requires a great deal more care than analog.
Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the
information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless.
Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? Without
constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps
historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replace analog.
As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the
night terrors of historians, and I’d be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution
currently exists. Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of
librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers
current and future. Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use
information. Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to
digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to
ply their trade, they won’t find it an impossible one.

【选项】
A)以偏概全
Hard work should be done to preserve artifacts. 用泛泛的 artifacts 代替「数字记录」，没有点出数字时代这个核心矛盾；且文章主线不是泛泛号召 hard work，而是揭示数字保存的难处与图书馆员角色。
B)以偏概全
Contributions of librarians should be recognized. 只截取第三段「图书馆员被低估」一面，没覆盖第四段 ZIP disk 例子与第五段表态；文章主旨是数字记录保存的挑战，图书馆员的贡献只是论证中的一环。
C)无中生有
Accessing databases is essential to researchers. 谈数据库访问的必要性；原文 universality of access 只是作为「用户低估图书馆」的引子，文章并未论证数据库访问对研究者的必要性。
D)✓ 正确
a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog↔Keeping digital historical records is a challenge.
I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists↔Keeping digital historical records is a challenge.
D 项把全文「难」+ 「可努力」的态度合在「a challenge」一个词里，覆盖 P2–P5 全部内容，且与作者既忧又持希望的口吻一致。

Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later.
第1段，第2句
“主句＋because 引导的原因部分”是非常常见、可迁移性很强的句式。再加上主句和从句都用主系表，属于阅读中高频出现的基础结构。
Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation?
第2段，第1句
“Given that”引导的原因背景以及“those who...”这种固定搭配在学术英语和真题中非常高频，具有很强的迁移价值。
For millennia, we've known what we've known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators' neglect.
第2段，第2句
本句成分丰富：主句包含主语、谓语、宾语（从句）、时间状语、原因状语；宾语从句内部有完整的主谓宾结构且 "what" 在从句内既是引导词又充当宾语，这是易错点；定语从句修饰名词，涉及关系代词的识别。此外，"due to" 引导的原因状语、"often despite" 引导的让步状语，覆盖多种状语类型。适合练习成分划分和从句识别。
At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on.
第2段，第4句
“时间状语 + 主句，yet + 主句 + 名词后接限定从句”是很常见的书面句式。掌握这种“并列主句中嵌定语从句”的读法，对处理考试长句很有迁移性。
Librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings.
第2段，第6句
“主句 + so that 引导的目的从句”是非常常见、可迁移的书面句式。掌握这种结构后，处理很多说明目的的英语句子都会更顺手。
The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
第2段，第7句
主句加非限制性定语从句的组合是四六级和考研阅读中的常见句式，定语从句补充说明前文内容的用法具有较高代表性。但整体结构相对简单，没有多层嵌套或复杂修饰，作为典型例句的覆盖面有限。
Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, "it's all in here" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today.
第3段，第1句
句子涵盖了主语（含所有格修饰）、谓语（情态动词结构、一般动词、系动词）、宾语、表语、方式状语（介词短语、动名词并列）、时间状语从句、同位语从句等多种成分。特别是"by + 动名词"的方式状语、同位语从句的识别、以及抽象名词"evidence"后接从句的搭配，都是练习中的高频易错点。
Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained?
第3段，第2句
疑问句 + 被动语态 + 并列结构是四六级和考研阅读中的高频组合。本句的'how + be + 主语 + 过去分词'模式在学术论证和说明文中极为常见，尤其在讨论机制、原因时频繁出现。两个疑问句并列且时态对比（过去 vs 现在）也是典型的论证句式。掌握本句结构后，可直接迁移到大量类似真题句，代表性很强。
When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one.
第3段，第4句
"When" 引导的状语从句 + 主句是四六级和考研阅读中的常见句式。"can be" 情态系动词结构也是高频考点。表语部分的 "if not... then" 对比表达在学术写作和阅读理解中时有出现。整体结构具有一定典型性，学习后可迁移到类似句型。
As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists.
第5段，第1句
这是学术和深度报道中非常典型的表达方式：先抛背景/身份，再接并列句表达观点，且使用了高频的虚拟假设句式。
Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future.
第5段，第2句
“主句表态度或判断 + in the fact that.../the fact that...” 是阅读中非常常见的书面结构。再加上里面嵌一个 "there are" 存在句，属于高度可迁移的典型句式。
While future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won't find it an impossible one.
第5段，第3句
让步状语从句加主句的 "While" 结构在四六级和考研阅读中频繁出现，是表达让步转折逻辑的典型句式。"find + 宾语 + 宾补" 结构也是常考的动词用法。掌握这个句子后，学生可以将让步从句的识别方法和宾补结构的分析技巧迁移到大量类似句子中
According to Paragraph 3, librarians' work may result in ________.
第38题题干
这是极为典型的阅读理解题干句式，掌握其“根据某段(According to...)，某物(Subject)会导致(result in)...”的结构对解题极有帮助。
Hard work should be done to preserve artifacts.
第40题，A
情态被动语态结构（should be done）和不定式作目的状语在考试中较为常见，具有一定代表性，掌握后可应用于类似表达建议或义务的句子，但简单句本身结构单一，迁移场景有限。
Accessing databases is essential to researchers.
第40题，C
结构具有较高典型性。动名词短语作主语的主系表结构在四六级和考研阅读中频繁出现，如 "Reading books is important" 或 "Understanding this concept is crucial to success"，掌握本句型可直接迁移到大量类似句式的理解和分析中。

questions.material:
A. Peters likes to photograph butterflies in a landscape, celebrating the beauty of their
surroundings as well as the insects themselves. His pictures of a Glanville fritillary rising from
the sea-pinks beside the chalk cliffs of Compton Bay on the Isle of Wight are particularly
glorious. These take-off shots are even more challenging because they require a wide-angle
lens, which means he must be less than 2cm from the butterfly. It’s incredibly difficult to get
that close to a skittish sun-warmed insect. Unlike some photographers, who “cheat” by keeping
insects in a fridge to slow them down, Peters refuses to tamper with wild butterflies.
B. Peters’ signature shot is a butterfly “take-off”, showing the multiple wing-beats of one
butterfly in one frame as it lifts off from a flower. How does he capture it? Technology helps.
A typical digital SLR camera shoots 20 frames a second. He uses a high-speed OM System
which shoots 120 frames a second.
C. Britain has relatively few butterfly species compared with mainland Europe and 80% are in
decline, mostly because intensive chemical farming has reduced many species to tiny
fragments of habitat and small nature reserves. Global heating is benefiting some species but
others are too isolated to find suitable new habitat, and gardening habits — paving over
gardens and using pesticides — aren’t helping either. Butterflies may not pollinate as many
plants as wild bees and hoverflies, but because British butterflies are the best-studied group of
insects in the world, they are an extremely useful indicator of the wider declines in flying
insects.
D. Five years ago, at summer’s end, Andrew Fusek Peters was diagnosed with bowel cancer. “I
was waiting for surgery, feeling really ill, sitting in my garden. It was amazing weather and
there were painted lady butterflies everywhere,” he says. “They were a symbol of fragile life,
of hope and defiance, and something appealed to my soul.”
E. That makes it sound easy, and artificial, but Peters insists it is still a massive challenge. He
typically takes between 10,000 and 20,000 shots to get one butterfly take-off sequence in focus.
At such high shutter speeds, the depth of field is tiny, and as butterflies do not fly in a straight
line they swiftly flutter out of focus. As well as thousands of attempts, it takes patience and
fieldcraft to anticipate a butterfly’s likely flight-line — and catch it — in focus.
F. So what’s the appeal of a long, sweaty day in pursuit of an elusive, fast-moving wild animal?
“It just feels bloody brilliant,” says Peters. “If I’ve had a full day of good encounters with
butterflies, met interesting butterfly people and I’ve got some good shots, that becomes a vault
in my spiritual bank. It’s a happy feeling.”
G. A children’s author and poet who had become a keen amateur photographer, Peters watched
the butterflies and idly wondered if he could capture them in flight. It swiftly became an
obsession as he recovered from a successful operation to remove the cancer. In recent
summers, he has travelled the length and breadth of Britain to photograph all 58 native species
of butterfly. Now the fruits of those summers have been published in a beautiful new book.
H. A butterfly takes off so quickly it is still impossible to react quickly enough to capture that
take-off but if he half-presses the shutter, the camera saves the 70 previous frames before the
moment he actually takes the picture. “It’s time travel, so I don’t miss the moment of take-off,”
he says. After he’s captured the butterfly taking off, he layers 10 to 15 frames together in
Photoshop.
41. → 42. → C → 43. → H → 44. → A → 45.

questions.material:
Innovation and research have relied on public participation in science for centuries. It was a
musician who discovered the planet Uranus in the 18th century by making his own telescope with
mirrors composed of copper and tin. (46) Recent decades have seen science move into a
convention where engagement in the subject can only be done through institutions, such as a
university. Citizen science provides an opportunity for greater public engagement and the
democratisation of science.
In the information era, large data sets, small teams and financial restrictions have slowed
scientific process. (47) But by utilising the natural curiosity of the general public it is possible to
overcome many of these challenges by engaging non-scientists directly in the research process.
Anyone can be a citizen scientist, regardless of age, nationality or academic experience. You don’t
even need any formal training, just an inquisitive mind and the enthusiasm to join one of the
thousands of citizen science projects to generate new knowledge and the means to understand a
genuine scientific outcome.
(48) Scientists have employed a variety of ways to engage the general public in their research,
such as making data analysis into an online game or sample collection into a smartphone
application. They’ve implored citizens to help with bug counting and categorising cancer cells,
and even identifying distant galaxies.
This form of accessible science means that great minds are able to join the race to create and
develop projects with the potential to change the world. A citizen science-based approach can
extend the field of vision and include different ideas and different brains to problem-solve and
create, making innovation faster and more effective.
The rise of citizen science has grown alongside the rise of do-it-yourself biology laboratories
around the world. (49) These groups of people are part of a rapidly expanding biotechnological
social movement of citizen scientists and professional scientists seeking to take discovery out of
institutions and put it into the hands of anyone with the enthusiasm.
There are around 40 official do-it-yourself biology centres across the globe in locations
including Paris, London, Sydney, and Tel Aviv. (50) They pool resources, collaborate, think
outside the box, and find solutions and ways around obstacles to explore science for the sake of
science without the traditional boundaries of working inside a formal setting. So is it time to take
the Petri dish out of the laboratory and into the garage?

I was really excited to hear that you’d invite some young craftsmen to demonstrate

Also, I’d like to help with your preparation work. Please let me know what I can do.
Yours,
Paul
questions.answer:
Dear Paul,
Thank you for your kind message and your warm interest in our craft demonstration.
You asked what the young craftsmen will show. They will present innovative works such as paper-cutting reshaped into modern greeting cards, and pottery decorated with bold digital-style patterns, blending old traditions with fresh creative ideas.

Looking forward to working together with you.
Yours,
Li Ming

Directions:
Write an essay of 160-200 based on the following table. In your essay, you should
1) describe the table briefly,
2) explain its intended meaning, and
3) give your comments.
You should write neatly on the ANSWER SHEET. (20 points)
年份 空调（台） 洗衣机（台） 电冰箱（台）
2014 75.2 83.7 85.5
2017 96.1 91.7 95.3
2020 117.7 96.7 101.8
2023 145.9 98.2 103.4
近年来全国居民平均每百户年末主要耐用消费品拥有量
questions.answer:
The table above clearly illustrates the changes in the average ownership of major durable consumer goods per 100 households across China from 2014 to 2023. As is shown, the ownership of air conditioners surged dramatically from 75.2 units to 145.9 units, nearly doubling over the decade, while washing machines and refrigerators rose only modestly, from 83.7 to 98.2 and from 85.5 to 103.4 respectively.
Several factors may account for this striking contrast. On the one hand, the rapid climb in air conditioners reflects Chinese residents' growing pursuit of a comfortable and higher-quality life as incomes steadily increase. On the other hand, washing machines and refrigerators, as long-standing household necessities, had already approached saturation, leaving limited room for further growth.
From my perspective, this trend is a vivid reflection of the remarkable improvement in people's living standards. To sustain such progress, the government and enterprises should continue to boost residents' incomes and produce more energy-efficient appliances, so that a better life becomes accessible to every family.
